protocol_type: Master-initiated, half-duplex, M-sequence-based UART protocol on the C/Q line. Each M-sequence is a Master message (Master Control octet selecting read/write and a communication channel + optional Process Data and/or On-request Data octets + a CKT checksum) followed by a Device response (optional data octets + a status octet + a CKS checksum). Acyclic parameters are addressed by the ISDU using an Index and Subindex.

control_strobes: RD / RD (read; either active edge works)
WR / WR (write; either active edge works)
host_bus_interface.address_strobe: ADS (latches A0-A2 + CS0-CS2 on positive edge if used; tie LOW if not needed)
host_bus_interface.buffer_disable_output: DDIS (LOW during CPU reads from UART)

rows: RBR (R) / THR (W) — Receiver Buffer / Transmitter Holding
IIR (R) / FCR (W) — Interrupt Identification / FIFO Control

channels_serial_side.name: SIN
channels_serial_side.description: Serial data input from peripheral/modem. Idle HIGH.

channels_serial_side.name: SOUT
channels_serial_side.description: Serial data output to peripheral/modem. Idle HIGH.

channels_serial_side.name: CTS
channels_serial_side.description: Clear to Send (active LOW); modem status only — does not gate transmitter.

channels_serial_side.name: RTS
channels_serial_side.description: Request to Send (active LOW); MCR bit 1.

channels_serial_side.name: DSR
channels_serial_side.description: Data Set Ready (active LOW); modem status.

channels_serial_side.name: DTR
channels_serial_side.description: Data Terminal Ready (active LOW); MCR bit 0.

channels_serial_side.name: DCD
channels_serial_side.description: Data Carrier Detect (active LOW); modem status.

valid_ready_handshake_rules: There is no per-byte ACK or VALID/READY handshake on the serial wire — UART is asynchronous with frame-level start/stop framing.
Host-bus side uses RD/WR strobes with stable A0-A2 + CS0-CS2.
Hardware flow control (when used): RTS asserted = UART ready to receive; CTS asserted = modem ready to receive. CTS does NOT gate transmitter directly — software interprets MSR.CTS.

frame_format.parity_bit: Optional; even / odd / stick (mark or space).
frame_format.stop_bits: 1, 1.5 (5-bit char only), or 2 bits, always HIGH.

frame_structure.purpose: Selects read/write, the communication channel (Process / Page / Diagnosis / ISDU), and the address.
Process Data Out and/or On-request Data from the Master.
6-bit checksum + 2-bit type/event field over the Master message.
Process Data In and/or On-request Data from the Device.
6-bit checksum + 2-bit type/event field over the Device response.

nibble_encoding.note: Each nibble pulse is measured falling-edge to falling-edge; value = (period_ticks - 12).

slow_serial_channel.name: Short Serial Message
slow_serial_channel.carrier: bit 2 (serial data) and bit 3 (start) of the status nibble.

slow_serial_channel.name: Enhanced Serial Message
slow_serial_channel.carrier: bit 2/3 of the status nibble across many frames.

spc_variant.name: SENT-SPC (Short PWM Code)
spc_variant.trigger: ECU drives a master trigger pulse on the signal line.
spc_variant.response: Sensor returns a standard SENT frame.
spc_variant.addressing: The master trigger pulse width can select which data channel the sensor returns (addressable).

crc.name: CRC-4
crc.coverage: data nibbles (and optionally the status nibble)
crc.method: 4-bit polynomial with a defined seed; lookup-table-based calculation.

addressing.on_wire: None — point-to-point, one Device per Master port.

m_sequence_types.name: TYPE_0
m_sequence_types.use: A single On-request Data octet per message; used in STARTUP.

m_sequence_types.name: TYPE_1
m_sequence_types.use: An On-request Data octet plus a small fixed Process Data length.

m_sequence_types.name: TYPE_2
m_sequence_types.use: Interleaved or larger Process Data with On-request Data; used in OPERATE for Devices with longer Process Data.

isdu.name: Indexed Service Data Unit
isdu.segmentation: An ISDU larger than one M-sequence payload is segmented across several M-sequences and reassembled.

checksum.ckt: Master-message checksum octet (6-bit checksum + 2-bit type/event field).
checksum.cks: Device-response checksum octet (6-bit checksum + 2-bit type/event field).
checksum.purpose: Data-integrity protection over the half-duplex link.
